chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'out of the food you feed your families with,' he said: It is as it happens; indeed, in the house there is one who eats more than a mud, and among them is one who eats less than a mud, so it is between that. And if you wish, you can make for them a ud'm (side dish/sauce), and the ud'm, its lowest is salt, its average is vinegar and oil, and its highest is meat.

key_terms.الْمُدِّ: a mud (a traditional unit of volume)

ai.seo_question: What is considered the 'average' food for expiation according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) contextualizes the Quranic term 'average' (awsat) in the expiation of oaths (Kaffarat al-Yamin) as a flexible standard based on the customary consumption of the household rather than a rigid fixed amount. He illustrates this spectrum by categorizing side dishes (ud'm), where salt represents the minimum, vinegar and oil the moderate average, and meat the upper limit, thereby allowing for practical adaptability in fulfilling religious obligations according to one's means and local customs.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:89] out of the food you feed your families with. Heasws said: ‘It is as if he happens to be like the one who happens to be in the house, one who eats more than the handful, and among them is one who eats less than the handful. So it is between that, and if he so desire to, he can make for them some (curry) sauce, and the sauce, the lowest of it is the salt, and the average is the vinegar, and the oil, and the high of it is the meat’.
en.sarwar: 7. Aii ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from af-Halabiy who has narrated the following: “This is about the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.

‘. . . it is of the average kind of food that you provide to your family.’ Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is just as it is at home. Certain people eat one mud (a certain measurement) and certain others less or in between. If you like you can prepare a certain kind of sauce, the least of which is salt, the middle is vinegar and oil, and of a high quality is meat.’”
